scoreBoardChallenge.hint: Check the JavaScript source files in Burp's HTTP history for hidden routes. Look for path definitions in the main.js bundle.
scoreBoardChallenge.celebrationText: You found the Score Board! This is the first step every pentester takes — reconnaissance pays off.

loginAdminChallenge.hint: Try terminating the SQL query after the email address using comment characters (--). The password check will be ignored entirely.
loginAdminChallenge.celebrationText: Admin access achieved via SQL Injection! You just bypassed authentication on a real application.

adminSectionChallenge.hint: Browse the application's JavaScript bundle in Burp's HTTP history. Look for route definitions that include 'admin' or 'administration'.
adminSectionChallenge.celebrationText: You accessed the Admin Section! Broken access control is OWASP's #1 vulnerability.

forgedFeedbackChallenge.hint: Intercept the feedback submission request in Burp. Look for a UserId parameter — can you change it to impersonate another user?
forgedFeedbackChallenge.celebrationText: Feedback forged! You exploited a Broken Access Control flaw by manipulating the request body.

basketAccessChallenge.hint: Intercept the API request that loads your shopping basket. The basket ID is in the URL — try changing it to access another user's basket.
basketAccessChallenge.celebrationText: You accessed another user's basket! IDOR vulnerabilities expose sensitive user data.

negativeOrderChallenge.hint: Intercept the order submission in Burp and modify the quantity to a negative number. The server may not validate it.
negativeOrderChallenge.celebrationText: You placed a negative order! Client-side validation alone is never enough.

confidentialDocumentChallenge.hint: Look for directory listings or publicly accessible files. Try navigating to /ftp on the Juice Shop. Some files should not be public.
confidentialDocumentChallenge.celebrationText: Confidential document retrieved! Sensitive files should never be in public directories.

errorHandlingChallenge.hint: Provoke an error by sending malformed input (like a single quote) to the REST API. The server should not expose stack traces.
errorHandlingChallenge.celebrationText: Error handling failure discovered! Stack traces reveal internal architecture to attackers.

exposedMetricsChallenge.hint: Many applications expose monitoring endpoints. Try common paths like /metrics or /prometheus. Nmap's http-enum script can find these.
exposedMetricsChallenge.celebrationText: Exposed metrics found! Internal monitoring endpoints should never be publicly accessible.

feedbackChallenge.hint: The feedback form has a rating field with a maximum value enforced by the UI. Use Burp to intercept and change the rating to 0.
feedbackChallenge.celebrationText: Zero-star feedback submitted! Client-side restrictions mean nothing to a proxy user.

forgedReviewChallenge.hint: Intercept a product review submission. Can you modify the author field to post a review as another user?
forgedReviewChallenge.celebrationText: Review forged! Missing server-side authorization lets attackers impersonate others.

loginBenderChallenge.hint: Use the same SQL injection technique from the admin login, but target Bender's email: bender@juice-sh.op
loginBenderChallenge.celebrationText: Bender's account compromised! Same technique, different target — SQL injection is devastating.

loginJimChallenge.hint: Jim's email is jim@juice-sh.op. Use SQL comment injection after the email to bypass the password check.
loginJimChallenge.celebrationText: Jim's account breached! Every account is vulnerable when SQLi exists.

passwordStrengthChallenge.hint: The admin has a weak password. Try common passwords or use Hydra with a small wordlist against the login API.
passwordStrengthChallenge.celebrationText: Weak password cracked! This is why password policies and MFA are critical.

privacyPolicyChallenge.hint: Look in the application's footer or about section. Sometimes privacy policies are linked from unexpected places.
privacyPolicyChallenge.celebrationText: Privacy Policy found! Reconnaissance includes reading all available documentation.

redirectChallenge.hint: Find a redirect endpoint in the application. Intercept it with Burp and modify the target URL to an external domain.
redirectChallenge.celebrationText: Open redirect exploited! These are used in phishing attacks to make malicious links look legitimate.

registerAdminChallenge.hint: Intercept the user registration request in Burp. Look for hidden parameters — can you add a 'role' field set to 'admin'?
registerAdminChallenge.celebrationText: Admin account registered! Mass assignment vulnerabilities let attackers set privileged fields.

repetitiveRegistrationChallenge.hint: Try registering with the same email twice. Does the application properly handle duplicate accounts, or can you bypass the check via Burp?
repetitiveRegistrationChallenge.celebrationText: Duplicate registration bypassed! Input validation must happen on the server side.

unionSqlInjectionChallenge.hint: Use a UNION SELECT payload in the search field. First determine the column count, then extract data from other tables.
unionSqlInjectionChallenge.celebrationText: UNION-based SQLi executed! You just extracted data from a completely different table.

weakPasswordChallenge.hint: Some users have extremely weak passwords. Think about the most common passwords people use — or use Hydra with rockyou.txt.
weakPasswordChallenge.celebrationText: Weak password exploited! The user chose a password from the top 100 most common list.

xssTierOneChallenge.hint: Try inserting a <script>alert('XSS')</script> tag into the search field or a user input that gets reflected on the page.
xssTierOneChallenge.celebrationText: Reflected XSS achieved! The application rendered your malicious script in the DOM.

xssTierTwoChallenge.hint: Look for stored XSS vectors — try injecting script tags into product reviews or feedback that persists across page loads.
xssTierTwoChallenge.celebrationText: Stored XSS executed! This is more dangerous than reflected XSS because it affects all visitors.

retrieveBlueprintChallenge.hint: Products may have associated files. Look for patterns in the /assets directory or try common file extensions (.stl, .obj) for product IDs.
retrieveBlueprintChallenge.celebrationText: Blueprint retrieved! Sensitive intellectual property was left in an accessible location.

changePasswordBenderChallenge.hint: Intercept the password change request. Is the current password verified? Can you change the request to target a different user?
changePasswordBenderChallenge.celebrationText: Password changed without authorization! CSRF and missing auth checks are a deadly combination.

csrfChallenge.hint: Craft a request to the change password endpoint without proper CSRF tokens. Use Burp Repeater to test if the server validates origin.
csrfChallenge.celebrationText: CSRF attack successful! The server failed to verify the request origin.

directoryListingChallenge.hint: Try browsing to /ftp on the Juice Shop. Directory listing may be enabled, exposing files that should be hidden.
directoryListingChallenge.celebrationText: Directory listing discovered! Server misconfigurations expose internal file structures.

httpHeaderXssChallenge.hint: Some XSS payloads can be delivered via HTTP headers. Use Burp to inject script tags into headers that get reflected in error pages.
httpHeaderXssChallenge.celebrationText: HTTP Header XSS executed! Even headers can be attack vectors when reflected unsanitized.

knownVulnerabilityChallenge.hint: Check the application's dependencies for known vulnerabilities. Look at package.json or use Nmap NSE scripts to fingerprint versions.
knownVulnerabilityChallenge.celebrationText: Known vulnerability exploited! Outdated dependencies are one of the most common attack vectors.

captchaBypassChallenge.hint: Intercept the CAPTCHA submission in Burp. Is the CAPTCHA validated server-side, or can you replay a valid response?
captchaBypassChallenge.celebrationText: CAPTCHA bypassed! Client-side CAPTCHA validation is trivially circumvented with a proxy.

loginMcSafeSearchChallenge.hint: MC SafeSearch's password is revealed in one of his songs/videos. Sometimes OSINT is more effective than brute force.
loginMcSafeSearchChallenge.celebrationText: MC SafeSearch compromised! Social engineering and OSINT can bypass technical controls.

domXssChallenge.hint: Try injecting an iframe or img tag with an onerror handler into the search field: <iframe src="javascript:alert('xss')"></iframe>
domXssChallenge.celebrationText: DOM-based XSS triggered! The client-side JavaScript unsafely processed your input.

ghostLoginChallenge.hint: A deleted user account may still exist in the database. Try SQL injection to log in as a user that no longer appears in the UI.
ghostLoginChallenge.celebrationText: Ghost login achieved! Soft-deleted accounts can be a hidden attack surface.

tokenSaleChallenge.hint: Look for hidden pages in the JavaScript bundle. There's a token sale page that isn't linked from the navigation.
tokenSaleChallenge.celebrationText: Token Sale page discovered! Hidden doesn't mean secure — security through obscurity fails.

/#/login.title: Login Page Detected
/#/login.body: This is a prime target for SQL Injection (Module 2) and Brute Force (Module 5). Try entering a single quote in the email field to test for SQLi.

/#/search.title: Search Functionality
/#/search.body: Search fields are common injection points. Try entering a single quote (') to provoke a database error, or use <script> tags for XSS testing.

/#/register.title: Registration Page
/#/register.body: Intercept the registration request with Burp. Look for hidden fields like 'role' that could be injected via mass assignment.

/#/basket.title: Shopping Basket
/#/basket.body: Check the API request for your basket ID. Try changing it to access other users' baskets (IDOR vulnerability).

/#/contact.title: Contact / Feedback Form
/#/contact.body: Feedback forms often have client-side restrictions. Use Burp to bypass rating limits or forge feedback as another user.

/#/score-board.title: Score Board
/#/score-board.body: You found the hidden score board! This tracks all Juice Shop challenges. Monitor it to see your progress.

/#/administration.title: Admin Panel
/#/administration.body: You've accessed the admin section! Look for user management, feedback moderation, and other privileged functions.

/#/forgot-password.title: Password Reset
/#/forgot-password.body: Password reset flows can be vulnerable. Check if security questions have guessable answers or if the reset token is predictable.

/#/order-history.title: Order History
/#/order-history.body: Order history pages may expose other users' orders through IDOR. Try manipulating the request to access different order IDs.

/#/privacy-security.title: Privacy & Security Settings
/#/privacy-security.body: Account settings pages often contain sensitive operations. Check if the password change requires current password verification.

Injection.description: Flaws that allow untrusted data to be interpreted as code or queries.

Broken Access Control.description: Failures in enforcing permissions, allowing unauthorized access to resources.

XSS.description: Cross-Site Scripting — injecting malicious client-side scripts into web pages.

Sensitive Data Exposure.description: Inadequate protection of sensitive data like credentials, tokens, or files.

Security Misconfiguration.description: Insecure default settings, incomplete configurations, or verbose error messages.

Broken Authentication.description: Weak authentication mechanisms allowing credential stuffing or session hijacking.

Miscellaneous.description: Challenges that don't fit neatly into a single OWASP category.

Cryptographic Issues.description: Weak or improperly implemented cryptographic protections.
